articles.standfirst: A eleição no Rio Grande do Norte foi a mais disputada no estado nos últimos 40 anos. Cadu de Lula, derrotou Allyson Bezerra, do União Brasil, por pouco mais de 32 mil votos.
articles.summary: A eleição no Rio Grande do Norte foi a mais disputada no estado nos últimos 40 anos. Cadu de Lula, derrotou Allyson Bezerra, do União Brasil, por pouco mais de 32 mil votos.
articles.body:
No Rio Grande do Norte, Cadu de Lula, do PT, foi eleito governador.

A eleição no Rio Grande do Norte foi a mais disputada no estado nos últimos 40 anos. Cadu de Lula, do PT, derrotou Allyson Bezerra, do União Brasil, por pouco mais de 32 mil votos.

Cadu tem 48 anos, é auditor fiscal do estado desde 2005. Em 2019, assumiu a Secretaria Estadual de Tributação do governo Fátima Bezerra, também do PT. Ele deixou o cargo em abril de 2026 para disputar a eleição, na primeira vez em que concorreu a um cargo eletivo.

Nesta segunda-feira (26), Cadu falou sobre a importância do diálogo para os desafios da gestão:

“Eu dialogo com todo mundo. Eu acho que é o momento da gente unir a classe política do nosso estado, quem votou e quem não votou, para a gente trabalhar para o povo. O povo vai às lutas votando para que ele seja atendido nas suas demandas, independente se a oposição, situação. Eu acho que tem que ter um compromisso agora com o povo do nosso Rio Grande do Norte, do nosso estado”.

articles.title: Rússia e Ucrânia suspendem ataques em Oleshky para ação humanitária; ataques continuam | G1
articles.standfirst: Trégua na cidade ocupada pela Rússia permitirá entrega de ajuda e retirada de moradores; novos ataques atingiram Kiev e outras cidades.
articles.summary: Trégua na cidade ocupada pela Rússia permitirá entrega de ajuda e retirada de moradores; novos ataques atingiram Kiev e outras cidades.
articles.body:
Imagem estática extraída de um vídeo de drone sem data, divulgado em 12 de setembro de 2026, mostra prédios destruídos em Oleshky , região de Kherson, Ucrânia controlada pela Rússia. — Foto: 34ª Brigada de Fuzileiros Navais "Borysfen"/Divulgação via Reuters

Rússia e Ucrânia iniciaram nesta terça-feira (27) um cessar-fogo regional para permitir uma operação humanitária em Oleshky, cidade do sul da Ucrânia ocupada pelas forças russas. Apesar da trégua na região, os dois países mantiveram ataques em outras áreas, incluindo Kiev, a capital ucraniana.

O cessar-fogo deve permitir a entrega de ajuda e a retirada de moradores de Oleshky, que enfrenta uma grave escassez de alimentos e medicamentos.

"Como chefe da equipe de negociação ucraniana, confirmo que o lado ucraniano está cumprindo seus compromissos", afirmou Dmytro Lubinets, comissário de Direitos Humanos do Parlamento da Ucrânia, em uma publicação no Facebook.

O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia informou que suspendeu os bombardeios na direção da cidade de Kherson a partir das 4h de Moscou, 22h de segunda-feira (26) no horário de Brasília, para permitir a preparação da operação humanitária em Oleshky.

Segundo Lubinets, o acordo foi alcançado em coordenação com a primeira-dama dos Estados Unidos, Melania Trump, e com Yana Lantratova, comissária de Direitos Humanos da Rússia.

Oleshky fica na margem leste do Rio Dnipro, na região de Kherson, em frente à cidade de mesmo nome, que está sob controle das forças ucranianas. Tropas russas controlam Oleshky desde os primeiros dias da invasão da Ucrânia, iniciada em fevereiro de 2022.

Apesar do cessar-fogo em Oleshky, novos ataques atingiram Kiev nesta terça-feira. A Ponte Sul e estruturas do metrô foram atingidas, segundo autoridades da cidade, e o trânsito precisou ser interrompido. Uma testemunha da Reuters relatou ter ouvido explosões.

Equipes de resgate ucranianas removem árvores caídas perto de um carro destruído em uma estrada em Kiev. — Foto: Genya Savilov/AFP

Desde a noite de segunda-feira (26), um ataque russo com mísseis contra Kiev deixou pelo menos uma pessoa morta e 15 feridas, entre elas estudantes que estavam em um alojamento. Ataques também deixaram mortos e feridos nas cidades de Kharkiv e Pavlohrad.

O Ministério da Defesa russo afirmou que atingiu a infraestrutura de transportes de Kiev, um centro logístico na região de Kharkiv, além de instalações industriais e navios de carga que, segundo Moscou, eram utilizados para fins militares.

Do lado russo, um ataque com drone matou um homem e deixou seis pessoas feridas na cidade de Bryansk, perto da fronteira com a Ucrânia.

Em outro ataque, uma pessoa morreu e 30 ficaram feridas após um drone atingir um ônibus em uma área da região de Zaporizhzhia controlada pela Rússia, segundo autoridades locais.

articles.title: Carreta tomba após colisão e fecha Ponte Rio-Niterói no sentido Rio | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu na altura do Vão Central e não deixou vítimas; equipes trabalham na limpeza da pista.
articles.summary: Acidente ocorreu na altura do Vão Central e não deixou vítimas; equipes trabalham na limpeza da pista.
articles.body:
Um acidente envolvendo dois caminhões interditou a Ponte Rio-Niterói, no sentido Rio de Janeiro, na noite de segunda-feira (26) e na madrugada desta terça-feira (27). Uma das carretas tombou e espalhou pela pista parte da carga de legumes que transportava.

O acidente aconteceu por volta das 22h34, na altura do Vão Central. Segundo a Ecovias Ponte, concessionária responsável pela via, um caminhão estava parado em uma faixa após apresentar uma pane quando foi atingido na traseira por outro veículo.

Com a colisão, uma das carretas tombou, bloqueando a pista. Imagens registradas no local mostram o veículo tombado e a carga de legumes espalhada pela via.

Segundo a concessionária, ninguém ficou ferido.

Todas as faixas no sentido Rio foram inicialmente interditadas. À 0h15, uma delas chegou a ser liberada para o tráfego, enquanto outras três permaneciam fechadas.

À 1h07, porém, todas as faixas voltaram a ser interditadas para a limpeza da pista e a chegada de recursos operacionais.

No sentido Niterói, o fluxo seguia normal. Na atualização das 1h07, o tempo de travessia era de 15 minutos.

articles.body:
No Amazonas, Omar Aziz, do PSD, venceu o segundo turno e voltará a governar o estado depois de 12 anos.

Omar Aziz, do PSD, passou o dia em casa, dedicado a articulações voltadas à transição e ao novo governo. Ele derrotou a candidata Professora Maria do Carmo, no PL, com quase 470 mil votos de vantagem.

Engenheiro civil, Omar começou a vida pública como deputado estadual. Foi vice-prefeito de Manaus, vice-governador, governador e está no segundo mandato como senador. Em 2021, presidiu a CPI da Covid.

Omar Aziz disse que terá auditores na transição e que vai priorizar a saúde para reduzir filas de espera para consultas, cirurgias e tratamentos:

"Hoje, eu estava analisando o nosso programa de governo, preciso me aprofundar nas pessoas que vão nos ajudar. A saúde não pode esperar, mas nós vamos, ao mesmo tempo, estar trabalhando em todas as áreas de atividade-fim que o Estado tem. São coisas que a gente já fez uma vez, dá para fazer de novo”.

articles.body:
Vicentinho Junior, do PSDB, foi eleito governador do Tocantins.

O Tocantins foi o primeiro estado a ter o governador definido no segundo turno. Vicentinho Júnior, do PSDB, venceu com 64% dos votos. A diferença para a segunda colocada, Professora Dorinha, do União Brasil, foi de 253 mil votos. Vicentinho Junior venceu as eleições de virada. Ele terminou o primeiro turno na segunda posição, com 13 mil votos a menos do que a adversária.

Vicentinho Junior tem 41 anos, é empresário e está no terceiro mandato consecutivo como deputado federal. Um dia depois da vitória, ele reforçou que uma das prioridades do governo será a segurança pública:

“Um estado que deixa o povo nosso sequestrado à criminalidade, você não permite esse estado prosperar. O estado prospera quando você dá um ambiente saudável de quem está nele gerando emprego e renda, de manter, ou de quem quer vir investir no nosso estado para o poder prover mais um pouco. E, feito isso, devolver altivez às nossas instituições".

articles.title: Projetistas apostam no contraste para criar cozinhas com identidade | G1
articles.standfirst: A combinação equilibrada de diferentes superfícies transforma materiais em parte da identidade do projeto.
articles.summary: A combinação equilibrada de diferentes superfícies transforma materiais em parte da identidade do projeto.
articles.body:
O ano de 2026 ficou marcado pelo retorno dos projetos afetivos. E as cozinhas, consideradas o coração da casa, mostram que unidade visual não significa repetir a mesma cor ou acabamento em todos os elementos. Pelo contrário, a identidade pode surgir justamente do encontro entre linguagens diferentes. Pedra, madeira, revestimentos decorativos e metais dividem o mesmo espaço, desde que exista equilíbrio entre desenho, tonalidade e proporção.

Esse resultado começa pela definição de uma hierarquia. Se a bancada apresenta veios marcantes, por exemplo, outros elementos podem assumir uma presença mais discreta. Quando a parede é o ponto de destaque, piso, marcenaria e metais podem funcionar como apoio. Determinar qual superfície terá maior peso visual ajuda a evitar excesso de informação.

O porcelanato Val Gardena Sabbia, da Villagres, traz a aparência da pedra em uma base clara e suave, criando continuidade entre bancada, piso e demais superfícies da cozinha sem sobrecarregar a composição — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

O Val Gardena Sabbia, da Villagres, exemplifica uma das possibilidades dessa linguagem. Inspirado na aparência da pedra, o porcelanato pode funcionar como ponto de partida para combinações que exploram diferentes texturas sem perder equilíbrio. Quando utilizado em áreas de maior destaque, como piso ou superfícies amplas, cria uma base mineral que pode ser acompanhada por madeira, marcenaria lisa e metais de desenho mais limpo.

A madeira, ou materiais que reproduzem sua aparência, entra com outro papel. Além de acrescentar calor visual, ajuda a aproximar a cozinha de salas de jantar e espaços de convivência. Essa presença não precisa dominar o ambiente. Piso, painel, marcenaria ou uma aplicação pontual já podem ser suficientes para estabelecer contraste com pedras e acabamentos mais frios.

O LVT Home Fasano Massima, da Biancogres, leva a aparência da madeira para o piso e cria contraste com superfícies de inspiração mineral — Foto: Acervo Vilarejo

Combinar materiais não significa utilizá-los na mesma quantidade. Uma cozinha pode ter um acabamento predominante, outro complementar e um terceiro reservado a pequenos pontos de destaque. Essa diferença de escala ajuda a organizar o olhar e evita que todos os elementos tenham a mesma intensidade.

As cores também participam desse equilíbrio. Superfícies diferentes podem compartilhar um mesmo subtom, criando continuidade mesmo quando apresentam texturas distintas. Em outras situações, o contraste pode ser mais evidente, desde que uma das tonalidades apareça de maneira mais controlada.

O mesmo raciocínio vale para desenhos e veios. Uma pedra de movimento intenso tende a ganhar mais destaque quando aparece ao lado de superfícies lisas. Já uma base mais uniforme permite trabalhar madeira, revestimentos com textura ou metais de maior presença sem tornar o conjunto pesado.

Metais entram como uma camada complementar. Cromado, dourado, grafite ou outros acabamentos podem acompanhar cores já presentes na cozinha ou criar um ponto de contraste. Torneiras, puxadores e acessórios não precisam necessariamente repetir exatamente a mesma tonalidade, mas devem estabelecer uma relação coerente com o restante do conjunto.

Na Vilarejo, reunir amostras durante a escolha ajuda a perceber como essas relações funcionam antes da aplicação. Colocar porcelanatos, revestimentos e outros acabamentos lado a lado permite observar diferenças de tom, desenho e textura que nem sempre ficam evidentes quando cada item é analisado isoladamente.

Uma cozinha ganha identidade quando os materiais cumprem papéis diferentes sem competir entre si. Pedra pode trazer presença, madeira pode aquecer, o metal pode pontuar e uma superfície mais neutra pode equilibrar o conjunto. É essa distribuição de funções, e não a repetição de um único acabamento, que permite construir uma composição mais interessante e coerente.

articles.title: Novas metas climáticas preveem corte de só 6% nas emissões, diz ONU | G1
articles.standfirst: Para limitar o aquecimento a 1,5°C, redução necessária seria de 60%. Projeções indicam que a temperatura média do planeta pode subir até 3,2°C neste século.
articles.summary: Para limitar o aquecimento global a 1,5°C, a redução necessária seria de 60% até 2035. Projeções indicam que a temperatura do planeta pode subir até 3,2°C neste século.
articles.body:
As novas metas climáticas apresentadas pelos países podem reduzir as emissões globais de gases de efeito estufa em apenas 6% até 2035 , um corte dez vezes menor do que o necessário para limitar o aquecimento global a 1,5°C.

O alerta vem da Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU), que afirma que, apesar dos compromissos assumidos desde a assinatura do Acordo de Paris, em 2015, o mundo continua distante de conseguir conter o aumento da temperatura do planeta.

A avaliação, divulgada nesta terça-feira (27) pela Convenção-Quadro das Nações Unidas sobre Mudança do Clima (UNFCCC), chega às vésperas da COP31, que será realizada entre 9 e 20 de novembro , em Antália, na Turquia.

O documento considera 127 novas metas climáticas nacionais , conhecidas como NDCs, apresentadas entre janeiro de 2024 e agosto de 2026.

Juntas, elas representam 154 participantes do Acordo de Paris , incluindo a União Europeia e seus países-membros, responsáveis por aproximadamente 71% das emissões globais registradas em 2019, sem considerar o desmatamento e as mudanças no uso da terra.

Segundo a ONU, mesmo que os novos compromissos sejam cumpridos, as emissões globais devem ficar, em média, apenas 6% abaixo dos níveis de 2019 até 2035.

Para manter o aquecimento limitado a 1,5°C, sem ultrapassar esse patamar ou com uma ultrapassagem pequena e temporária, as emissões precisariam cair aproximadamente 60% no mesmo período , de acordo com as estimativas do Painel Intergovernamental sobre Mudanças Climáticas (IPCC).

🌡️ ENTENDA: Essa meta de 1,5°C foi estabelecida pelo Acordo de Paris em 2015 para evitar impactos extremos do clima, como secas, elevação do mar e colapso de geleiras. Estudos recentes, porém, mostram que o mundo pode já ter ultrapassado esse ponto crítico.

Para limitar o aumento da temperatura a menos de 2°C , a redução necessária seria de aproximadamente 37% .

A ONU calcula ainda que, se todas as medidas previstas nas novas metas forem integralmente implementadas, incluindo aquelas que dependem de financiamento e apoio internacional, a redução poderia chegar a 9% até 2035 .

📝ENTENDA: Essas metas são o principal instrumento do Acordo de Paris para enfrentar a crise climática. A NDC atual do Brasil, por exemplo, inclui a meta de reduzir as emissões de gases de efeito estufa em 53% até 2030 e zerar as emissões líquidas até 2050.

Sem essas medidas adicionais, a queda seria de apenas 3%. Apesar da distância em relação aos objetivos do acordo, o documento aponta que as emissões globais podem atingir seu pico antes de 2030 e começar a diminuir nos anos seguintes.

A projeção indica que o volume anual de gases de efeito estufa deve ficar entre 49,6 bilhões e 55,9 bilhões de toneladas de CO2 equivalente em 2035. Essa medida permite somar diferentes gases, considerando o potencial de aquecimento de cada um.

A redução prevista, porém, ainda seria insuficiente para impedir que o planeta ultrapasse o limite de 1,5°C.

Com base nas novas metas nacionais e nas projeções para as emissões futuras, o aquecimento global pode chegar a 3,2°C até o fim do século.

Por que cada grau importa? — Foto: Gui Sousa/Arte g1

O documento estima um aumento da temperatura entre 2,1°C e 3,2°C até 2100 , considerando os compromissos apresentados e as hipóteses utilizadas para projetar as emissões após o período coberto pelas metas.

A ONU apresenta também uma segunda estimativa, que considera os objetivos de longo prazo dos países, incluindo as promessas de zerar as emissões líquidas de gases de efeito estufa até meados do século.

Nesse caso, o aquecimento projetado ficaria entre 1,7°C e 2,3°C até 2100.

Para que essa projeção se confirme, porém, os países precisarão cumprir as metas de longo prazo e adotar medidas para reduzir as emissões nas próximas décadas.

O relatório também alerta que o mundo pode esgotar antes de 2030 o limite de emissões de CO₂ considerado compatível com a meta de restringir o aquecimento global a 1,5°C.

Segundo a ONU, esse limite, chamado de orçamento de carbono, é de aproximadamente 130 bilhões de toneladas de CO₂ a partir do início de 2026. O volume equivale a cerca de três anos das emissões globais atuais.

A previsão, no entanto, é que os países emitam aproximadamente 368 bilhões de toneladas de CO₂ entre 2026 e 2035, considerando os compromissos apresentados até agora. O volume é quase três vezes maior que o limite disponível para manter o aquecimento em 1,5°C.

Com isso, caso a temperatura global ultrapasse esse patamar, seria necessário remover grandes quantidades de CO₂ da atmosfera para tentar reduzir o aquecimento novamente.

Chaminés industriais liberam fumaça na atmosfera, uma das fontes de poluição do ar e de emissão de gases que contribuem para o aquecimento global. — Foto: Adina Voicu/Pixabay

Apesar dos resultados, a ONU reconhece que os governos passaram a incluir mais medidas de enfrentamento às mudanças climáticas em suas metas nacionais.

Cerca de 90% dos participantes analisados afirmaram ter considerado as conclusões do primeiro balanço global do Acordo de Paris, concluído na COP28, realizada em Dubai, em 2023 .

Além disso, 99% apresentaram medidas nacionais para reduzir emissões, principalmente nos setores de energia, transporte, indústria, agricultura e gestão de resíduos.

Ainda segundo a análise da ONU, a transição energética está entre as principais prioridades dos países.

A parcela que apresentou medidas para modernizar as redes elétricas passou de 51% para 70%, enquanto a proporção dos que preveem ampliar o armazenamento de energia subiu de 33% para 56% .

O relatório também aponta que 92% dos participantes incluíram o metano em suas metas climáticas e 90% apresentaram compromissos relacionados ao uso da terra e às florestas, como o combate ao desmatamento e o reflorestamento.

Apesar das novas promessas, os resultados ainda são desiguais. Um segundo relatório divulgado nesta terça-feira, com base em 137 documentos nacionais, mostra que 61 participantes registraram avanços em direção às metas climáticas, enquanto outros 27 se afastaram dos objetivos ou apresentaram resultados mistos.

A ONU ressalta que esses avanços não significam, necessariamente, que os países estejam reduzindo suas emissões no ritmo necessário para cumprir os compromissos.

Consequências do aquecimento global — Foto: Gui Sousa/Arte g1

A adaptação aos efeitos das mudanças climáticas também ganhou espaço nas novas metas.

Segundo a ONU, 86% dos participantes incluíram medidas nessa área, principalmente para proteger a produção de alimentos, os recursos hídricos e a saúde, além de prevenir desastres.

Entre esses países, 92% também mencionaram perdas e danos provocados pelas mudanças climáticas, como destruição de infraestrutura, prejuízos econômicos e mortes em eventos extremos. Nas metas anteriores, essa proporção era de 56%.

Apesar disso, a implementação das medidas ainda enfrenta dificuldades. Até outubro de 2026, 81 países em desenvolvimento haviam apresentado planos nacionais de adaptação, mas 36 dos 41 planos analisados entre países menos desenvolvidos e pequenos Estados insulares ainda estavam nas etapas iniciais de execução.

O financiamento também continua sendo um obstáculo. Os investimentos climáticos globais chegaram a uma média de US$ 1,9 trilhão por ano em 2023 e 2024 , um aumento de 32% em relação ao biênio anterior.

Desse total, apenas 9% foram destinados a transferências internacionais para países em desenvolvimento, o equivalente a cerca de US$ 183 bilhões anuais.

Os recursos voltados especificamente à adaptação somaram US$ 63 bilhões por ano , uma queda de 20% e apenas 3% do financiamento climático global identificado.

Já os países desenvolvidos superaram, em 2023 e 2024, a promessa de mobilizar US$ 100 bilhões anuais para apoiar nações em desenvolvimento. Os valores chegaram a US$ 132,8 bilhões e US$ 136,7 bilhões , respectivamente. A meta, no entanto, deveria ter sido cumprida originalmente em 2020.

A contabilização desses recursos ainda é motivo de divergência. Segundo a Oxfam, o esforço financeiro efetivo dos países ricos em 2024 ficou entre US$ 32,7 bilhões e US$ 44,7 bilhões, considerando critérios diferentes dos utilizados pela OCDE.

articles.title: Sono: o agente modificador das doenças neurodegenerativas  | G1
articles.standfirst: Durante a vigília, a atividade cognitiva tem um custo; é quando dormimos que o cérebro repara danos e elimina neurotoxinas.
articles.summary: Durante a vigília, a atividade cognitiva tem um custo; é quando dormimos que o cérebro repara danos e elimina neurotoxinas.
articles.body:
Chego à quarta e última coluna inspirada nas palestras a que assisti no XXXII Congresso Brasileiro de Neurologia (Neuro 2026). O tema é um dos meus favoritos por estar intrinsecamente ligado ao envelhecimento ativo: o sono. Costumo dizer que temos, todas as noites, a oportunidade de visitar um spa gratuito para nos renovar – e não estou sozinha nessa percepção. “Proteger o sono é proteger a arquitetura do cérebro”, resumiu o neurologista Raimundo Nonato Delgado Rodrigues, professor associado da Universidade de Brasília e uma referência nacional no assunto.

O sono funciona como um agente modificador das doenças neurodegenerativas; é quando dormimos que o cérebro repara danos e elimina neurotoxinas — Foto: daha3131053 para Pixabay

O médico recorreu à célebre máxima “Penso, logo existo”, criada pelo filósofo francês René Descartes, para sintetizar a importância do repouso: “Lembro, logo durmo”. E o que isso significa na prática? Na verdade, o sono é um poderoso agente modificador no curso das doenças neurodegenerativas.

Durante a vigília, ou seja, quando estamos acordados, a atividade cognitiva tem um custo molecular. O funcionamento sináptico gera microlesões genômicas, como as quebras na fita dupla de DNA, que demandam reparo especializado. O “conserto neuronal” se dá durante o sono, acompanhado por um processo fluido de depuração que bem poderíamos chamar de “lavagem noturna”. Enquanto estamos despertos, o espaço intersticial (entre as células) fica comprimido, acumulando resíduos metabólicos. No sono profundo, o sistema glinfático é ativado e esse espaço se expande, permitindo que o líquido cefalorraquidiano circule com mais facilidade, lavando e drenando as toxinas.

Quando ocorre a fragmentação do sono – típica em quadros de insônia ou na Síndrome da Apneia Obstrutiva do Sono – a remoção de agregados neurotóxicos, como beta-amiloide e tau hiperfosforilada, fica prejudicada. O desfecho a longo prazo é a elevação do risco de demências, notadamente a Doença de Alzheimer.

Instaura-se, então, um ciclo vicioso: o estresse oxidativo e o acúmulo proteico aceleram o dano neuronal e desorganizam ainda mais os centros reguladores do sono, perpetuando o declínio cognitivo. Na Doença de Parkinson, por exemplo, alterações expressivas no sono surgem comumente anos antes das primeiras manifestações motoras. Resumo da ópera: D-U-R-M-A-M!

articles.title: Just 3k turn up at last special SIR camp for inclusion of names in Delhi voter rolls
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The last round of special camps organised at nearly 15,000 polling stations across Delhi on Sunday under the ongoing special intensive revision
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The last round of special camps organised at nearly 15,000 polling stations across Delhi on Sunday under the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls drew a tepid response, with only 3,000-odd people submitting Form-6 applications for inclusion of their names in the rolls.Around 1,000 applications were received together through Form 7, for deletion of existing entries, including those of deceased voters, and Form 8, used for corrections in name, address etc, said officials.The camps were organised to provide additional opportunities to eligible voters whose names were deleted from the draft electoral rolls published on Aug 31. As many as 47.6 lakh out of 1.4 crore voters were deleted from the draft SIR rolls.Against this number, only 2.6 lakh Form-6 applications for inclusion of names have been received between Aug 31 and Oct 25, shows latest data released by the office of the chief electoral officer.West district records highest number of Form-6 applicationsDuring the same period, 19,804 Form-7 applications were submitted for deletion of names or objections to existing entries, while 99,720 Form-8 applications were received for corrections. Another 466 Form-6A applications were received from overseas electors for inclusion.The final round of special voter enrolment camps was organised ahead of the Oct 30 deadline. “BLOs were available at the nearly 15,000 polling stations on Oct 25 for the last special camp to help voters fill the related forms. Although a good number of people turned up at the locations, only 4,000 people submitted Forms 6, 7 and 8,” said an official.“We have made all efforts to ensure that no eligible voter is left behind. The response is understandable because those who wanted to submit forms for inclusion may already have done it during the two months long period from Aug 31 to Oct 30. Those who wish to submit their forms can do it till Friday (Oct 30) after which forms under SIR will not be accepted.” The 2.6 lakh Form 6 applications include voters whose names were deleted from draft SIR rolls and new voters.Among the 13 revenue districts, West recorded the highest number of Form-6 applications at 32,321, followed by North West (26,661), East (25,433), South East (25,293) and North East (25,241). New Delhi recorded the lowest number at 4,688.South West recorded the highest number of Form-7 applications at 3,013, followed by South (2,701), North East (2,400) and West (2,242). articles.summary: GUWAHATI: Arunachal Pradesh Congress president and former education minister Bosiram Siram on Monday alleged that Chinese troops have intruded 40 to 50 km
articles.body: GUWAHATI: Arunachal Pradesh Congress president and former education minister Bosiram Siram on Monday alleged that Chinese troops have intruded 40 to 50 km deep into Indian territory in Upper Subansiri district.However, denying the claim, CM Pema Khandu said he did not believe any incursion was taking place.Siram said a Congress delegation led by him visited border areas from Aug 26 to 29, travelling from Itanagar via Nacho to Limeking and Taksing, and spoke with local residents. The delegation included Congress working president and former home minister Tanga Byaling and Upper Subansiri MP Jarodum Kri.Thorough probe must be conducted: SiramThe Chinese PLA have already advanced 40 to 50 km into Indian territory. Today, Chinese PLA personnel are stationed up there, at intervals. You can see the Army. They are on top of the mountains, while we are down below," Siram said.In June, a local group, Nah Welfare Society, first raised the flag saying the PLA had expanded its presence near Taksing, a claim that the Indian Army said was "incorrect and without any basis". In Aug, a People's Party of Arunachal team claimed that Indian patrols were being denied access to key points.Union minister Kiren Rijiju rejected a 60-km intrusion claim, but acknowledged increased Chinese activity on the high ridges.Responding to govt's denials, Siram asked, "If no intrusion or aggressive activity has occurred on the border, why are residents repeatedly raising these complaints? Instead of brushing off these allegations merely as rumours, a thorough and impartial factual investigation must be conducted."Siram also cited recent remarks by ITBP Director General Shatrujit Singh Kapoor on face-off locations, and said the ground reality reported by locals warrants a transparent, high-level probe by the Centre and the defence ministry."Serious border-related issues should not be ignored by dismissing them as allegations or rumours. The facts must be established to ensure the security of the country's borders and protect the rights and livelihoods of people living in border areas," he said."Entire areas have reportedly disappeared from the online maps and have come under its control. The whole of Asaphila has come under its control. And the strategically important areas, including the high ground, have already been taken over by China. They are under Chinese occupation."We are seriously concerned about the Chinese incursions and the situation along the India-China border. During our visit to the border areas, we found that the situation needs to be examined carefully," Siram added.He alleged that aggressive activity by the Chinese PLA has disrupted lives and traditional livelihoods of locals."The central govt and the ministry of defence must take immediate steps to ensure border security and protect the rights, livelihoods and traditionally used areas of residents....," he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.summary: Jordan carried out airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria on Tuesday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in the
articles.body: Jordan carried out airstrikes against armed groups in southern Syria on Tuesday in retaliation for a deadly attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in the Jordanian city of Karak last week, with Syrian authorities reporting at least 7 civilian deaths.Syria’s civil defence agency said seven people were killed in strikes across the southern provinces of Daraa and Sweida. Among them were five members of a family, including three children and a woman, who died when a strike hit a tent in rural Daraa. Three other family members were injured. Two elderly men, aged 80 and 60, were killed in separate strikes, the agency said.Jordan’s air force said the operation killed and wounded several members of the targeted groups and destroyed multiple vehicles. However, it did not identify the groups or disclose the exact locations of the strikes.The Syrian government said the operation was conducted without prior coordination or notification. It said authorities were investigating the incident and had opened communication channels with Jordan to discuss the matter, news agency AP reported.Syria subsequently announced the closure of its main border crossing with Jordan.The strikes came after a gun attack on a Greek Orthodox Church in Karak on Friday killed nine people and wounded more than two dozen others. The attack took place during a funeral in the city, about 90 km south of the Jordanian capital, Amman.Jordanian authorities on Monday arrested three men in connection with the attack following a shootout at dawn. All three were wounded during the operation and taken into custody in Karak.The public security directorate identified the suspects as brothers Hazzah Zaidan Mohammad and Mishal Zaidan Mohammad, and their brother-in-law Ahmad Sami Hussein. All three are Jordanian nationals.The agency’s chief, Major General Obaidallah Abd Rabbo Al-Maayta, described the attackers as “takfiri”, a term commonly used for Sunni militants who label others as apostates. However, he said they were not linked to any organised group and acted on their own. Authorities also recovered a large cache of ammunition from the abandoned house where the men were apprehended.Interior minister Mazen Al-Faraya attributed the attack to extremist ideology, warning that similar incidents could recur if such thinking was not addressed.King Abdullah II had ordered authorities to respond firmly to those responsible, saying that the perpetrators would not escape punishment and that ideologies threatening national unity would not be tolerated.You use AI every day. articles.title: How a WhatsApp channel called ‘Lula’s Army’ became a force in Brazil election
articles.summary: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won Brazil’s presidential runoff, securing a fourth non-consecutive term after a closely contested election.
articles.body: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won Brazil’s presidential runoff, securing a fourth non-consecutive term after a closely contested election. However, the result faces a potential legal challenge from rival Flávio Bolsonaro, while US president Donald Trump has questioned the vote, alleging that it was “rigged”.Lula secured more than 64 million votes, defeating Bolsonaro, who received just under 60 million, by nearly 4.4 million votes. The incumbent is expected to take office on January 5, 2027, for a fourth non-consecutive term.A key factor in Lula’s comeback was the mobilisation of voters who had abstained in the first round or backed other candidates. An additional 14.1 million voters participated in the runoff, with analysts estimating that three-quarters of these votes went to Lula.Central to the campaign was lawmaker André Janones’ WhatsApp channel, “Lula’s Army”, which attracted nearly 11 million people and encouraged supporters to campaign on social media.Janones adopted an aggressive, sustained digital strategy, Oliver Stuenkel, a professor of international relations at Fundação Getulio Vargas in São Paulo told news agency AP.“He basically embraced the right’s style of aggressive politics, very intense, constant messaging,” Stuenkel said.“The defeat in the first round jolted the Lula campaign into action. The strategy during the first round was lacklustre and saw a lot of infighting,” he added, according to AP.Juliano Cortinhas, an international relations professor at the University of Brasília, said the digital campaign also helped pressure Meta, which owns WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook, over allegations of bias favouring Bolsonaro.“There was ‘external interference we were suffering by major platforms’,” Cortinhas told AP. He added: “It wasn't only Meta, many others were using their algorithms to repost many images and many messages of the far-right, and they did not do the same to the left.”Brazil’s top electoral court ruled on October 15 that Meta must ensure equal treatment of both candidates. The company subsequently said it had addressed the order.Meanwhile, Trump questioned the result on Monday, saying, “Elections have to be indisputable and it looked very bad to me.” He added: “I thought it had a very bad look, the way it was tabulated.”“It looked like another rigged election, frankly,” Trump said, without presenting evidence.Flávio Bolsonaro has pledged to organise opposition to Lula and seek to nullify the results. He said, “I am going to gather elected lawmakers and senators to organize our strategy and make the lower house and the Senate our fortress against barbaric acts that are set to happen in another four years of Lula.”However, overturning the result would require evidence of fraud affecting Lula’s 4.4 million-vote margin and approval from Brazil’s eight-member electoral court before certification on December 18.Benjamin Gedan, director of the Stimson Center’s Latin America programme, warned, “False claims of fraud are becoming commonplace, though that does not make them any less dangerous.”You use AI every day. articles.title: Can Netanyahu survive another storm? Israel votes after October 7, Gaza and Iran wars
articles.summary: Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing a crucial test of his political future in Tuesday's election, with voters weighing his leadership
articles.body: Israel Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is facing a crucial test of his political future in Tuesday's election, with voters weighing his leadership following the Hamas-led October 7, 2023, attacks, successive wars in Gaza and with Iran, and Israel's growing international isolation, news agency Reuters reported.Despite the mounting challenges, Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving leader with 19 years in office, remains a formidable political survivor. With nationalist politics firmly entrenched and the country's fragmented electoral system making coalition-building decisive, he could still emerge best placed to form the next government.Opinion polls point to a close contest between Netanyahu's Likud party and its right-wing allies and a rival alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff and security hawk who has attracted support from both right-wing and centrist voters.Netanyahu has made his wartime leadership and close relationship with US President Donald Trump central to his campaign. Trump has endorsed the Israeli leader, with the two countries joining forces in the war against Iran.On Sunday, Netanyahu said Trump was prepared to act again to “finally” remove the Iranian threat, but only if he remained in power. Eisenkot, however, accused the prime minister of "relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies and threats," adding that Trump would work "in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people."Netanyahu may once again need the support of far-right leaders Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich to secure a governing majority. Both have faced sanctions from some Western countries over allegations of inciting violence against Palestinians. Meanwhile, Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party has gained ground in opinion polls.Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot has a clear route to power. If neither manages to assemble a coalition in Israel's 120-member parliament, Netanyahu could remain in office as caretaker prime minister until another election is held next year.Polling stations are scheduled to remain open from 7 am to 10 pm (0500 to 2000 GMT).The October 7 reckoningThe election comes after one of the most turbulent periods in Israel's history since its establishment in 1948. The trauma of the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attacks, Israel's subsequent military offensive in Gaza and deep divisions over Netanyahu's right-wing government have dominated the country's political landscape.For many of Netanyahu's opponents, the vote is also a referendum on accountability for the security failures that preceded October 7, Israel's deadliest day.Mali Hajaj, an education ministry employee who supports Eisenkot, said a national inquiry into the attacks was essential for the country to begin healing."the most important thing is the establishment of a national inquiry because that's where our healing will come from," she said.Lisa Tortor, another voter opposed to Netanyahu, said she hoped he would leave office and a new government would begin repairing the damage to Israel's international standing and the wider Jewish community.She said she hoped Netanyahu would go and "they can form a new government and do some of the repairing of the damage that Bibi has done for Jews all over the world and for Israel, and Israel's image."Not all voters, however, believe the prime minister should be held responsible for the October 7 attacks. Nof Gabay, an 18-year-old Likud supporter, dismissed that criticism and backed Netanyahu's leadership during the war.Gabay called him "the right man for the state of Israel" and said, "Netanyahu managed the war in the best possible way."Netanyahu's wartime record under scrutinyThe election campaign has unfolded against the backdrop of years of military conflict that have reshaped Israel's security and diplomatic position.After the October 7 attacks, in which Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took another 251 hostage, Israel launched a military offensive that devastated much of Gaza. Gaza health authorities say Israeli attacks have killed 74,000 people.Israel also dealt major blows to Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon and exchanged strikes with Iran before launching a 12-day aerial campaign against Iranian nuclear sites in 2025. The conflict escalated further this year with a joint US-Israeli war against Iran.Netanyahu has presented his handling of these conflicts as evidence of his leadership and ability to confront Israel's security threats. His alliance with Trump has also become a key part of his pitch to voters, particularly as tensions with Iran remain central to the campaign.Eisenkot, meanwhile, has argued that Israel's next government must ensure Iran does not acquire a military nuclear capability. He has said this could be achieved through military action or an "arrangement", including a diplomatic solution backed by the United States.The competing positions underline how security policy remains central to the election, even as voters grapple with questions about accountability, the future of the Gaza conflict and Israel's standing abroad.Coalition arithmetic could decide the outcomeEven if Eisenkot's alliance makes gains, forming a government could prove difficult. Like nearly all Jewish-led parties in Israel, his camp opposes the two-state solution that has underpinned decades of peace negotiations with the Palestinians.Eisenkot has, however, criticised violence by Jewish settlers against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank. Such violence has surged since 2023, straining Israel's ties with Western countries. He has also opposed Netanyahu's far-right coalition partners, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich.Meanwhile, dissatisfaction with Netanyahu has prompted some voters in traditional Likud strongholds to campaign against him. Others have turned away from the prime minister as he continues to fight corruption charges in a long-running criminal trial, which he denies.The participation of Israel's Arab minority could also influence the outcome. Arab citizens of Israel, who are Palestinian by heritage, could help shift the balance in a closely contested election if turnout is high.Although Eisenkot has ruled out partnering with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values, analysts believe they could still support a minority government led by him. Such an arrangement could offer a route to removing Netanyahu from office without formally joining his coalition.The country's fragmented political system means that winning the most votes may not be enough. The ability to secure support from smaller parties and assemble a parliamentary majority could ultimately determine who governs Israel.Israeli political analyst Amotz Asa-El of the Shalom Hartman Institute expects the result to be closely fought, with neither side securing a decisive mandate."My expectation is that we will have only a slight majority either way. No landslide," Asa-El said, according to Reuters.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: US President Donald Trump’s public approval rating rose by one percentage point to 32 per cent, a slight recovery from last week’s record low, according
articles.body: US President Donald Trump’s public approval rating rose by one percentage point to 32 per cent, a slight recovery from last week’s record low, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.Trump’s Republican Party is fighting to keep control of Congress in the November 3 midterm elections.In the five-day nationwide poll, registered voters preferred Democrats to Republicans by 47 per cent to 36 per cent when asked which party they would back for Congress. This 11-point gap was one percentage point smaller than in the previous Reuters/Ipsos poll, which closed on October 19.When undecided voters were asked which party they were leaning towards, the Democratic lead shrank further to nine percentage points, with 50 per cent favouring Democrats and 41 per cent Republicans.Republicans currently hold majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate. Losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump’s agenda during the last two years of his second term, Reuters reported.The poll also pointed to a change in voters’ views on economic management. Reuters/Ipsos surveys beforethe war had shown voters preferring Republicans over Democrats on the economy. In the latest poll, 37 per cent of voters said Democrats had a better approach to the economy, against 33 per cent who favoured Republicans.Democratic voters also reported more enthusiasm about the midterms. About 46 per cent of Democrats said they were very enthusiastic about voting, compared with 30 per cent of Republicans.Generic ballot polls show which party voters would prefer to control Congress nationwide. However, they do not show how individual states and constituencies are likely to vote, which ultimately determines control of the House and Senate. Republicans have some structural advantages in these local contests, Reuters reported.The online Reuters/Ipsos poll surveyed 1,679 US adults, including 1,280 registered voters. The margin of error was two percentage points for all adults and three percentage points for registered voters.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Days after merger with Warner Bros, Skydance offers employees voluntary buyout; makes 5-day work-from-office compulsory across company; read full memo
articles.summary: Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreitz are overhauling the company’s corporate culture and cost structure, mandating a full five-day return to the
articles.body: Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreitz are overhauling the company’s corporate culture and cost structure, mandating a full five-day return to the office while launching a voluntary buyout programme for employees. The directives, detailed in an internal staff memo obtained by Deadline, mark the first major operational shake-up since Skydance finalised its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery weeks ago.Under the new policy, employees will be required to work on-site five days a week, phased in over time depending on location. The mandate aligns the broader workforce with Paramount-Skydance, which had already ended hybrid arrangements, while ending the three-day in-office model previously held at Warner Bros. Discovery. The transition will primarily affect major hubs in Los Angeles, New York, Atlanta, and London.“We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people,” Ellison and Kreitz wrote in the memo. “We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.”Alongside the in-office mandate, leadership introduced a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program aimed at reducing headcount as the company tackles a daunting balance sheet. The merged entity is saddled with nearly $90 billion in debt amid a climate of rising interest rates. Ellison has pledged to deliver at least $2 billion in cost savings, with significant reductions expected to come from layoffs.“As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that,” the memo stated. “To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.”Eligible employees are expected to receive their buyout packages in the coming days as Skydance accelerates its post-merger integration. Here's the full memo as it appeared in Deadline:Team,At Skydance, our goal is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology. We are creative-first, audience focused, tech-forward and globally scaled. And in a world of endless choice and fierce competition for attention, we don’t just want to succeed. We want to win.To do that, we must be a strong, connected and agile company. Among our business and creative priorities, none matters more than building a strong culture, because it’s the foundation of everything we want to achieve. Winning requires us to work as one team: one company, fully aligned. That means communicating openly and collaborating efficiently across every part of the organization.In-Person CollaborationWe believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems. Being together isn’t just about showing up. It’s about inspiring one another, learning and coaching, forming friendships and having the casual conversations that spark something great.With that in mind, we will adopt a five-day in-office policy across all of Skydance. We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.While many of you are already in the office five days a week, we understand this may be a significant change to the daily routines of others. To give you time to plan and adjust, we will take a phased approach by location. You will receive ample notice before changes take effect, and we will work closely with managers to support you through the transition.Voluntary Buyout ProgramAs we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.We recognize this is a significant decision, and we want you to feel informed and supported. If this applies to you, please review your materials carefully and reach out to your leadership or HR representative with any questions. FAQs and other resources are available on the Skydance Integration or Ask Employee Connection on WBD One.Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. We have the talent, the creative firepower and the ambition to do it, and we will get there together.Thank you for your commitment, and for the creativity and passion you bring to your work every day.Best,David and YnonYou use AI every day. articles.title: Convicted murderer serving life escapes through Tennessee prison fence, uses stolen truck as getaway vehicle, officials say
articles.summary: A 28-year-old convicted murderer serving a life sentence escaped through a Tennessee prison’s fence Sunday evening before stealing a truck and driving off —...
articles.body:
A 28-year-old convicted murderer serving a life sentence escaped through a Tennessee prison's fence Sunday evening before stealing a truck and driving off — and has not yet been located, according to Tennessee authorities.

Around 11:30 p.m. on October 25, staff at the Northwest Correctional Complex learned Jacob Morley was missing, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. He had been sentenced to life in prison after being convicted of first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism.

Security camera footage later revealed Morley "breached the perimeter fence" and left the facility wearing his prison uniform, the department said. It remains unclear how he escaped through the fence.

Video obtained by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation shows Morley stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350 with Tennessee plates around 1 a.m. on October 26, the agency said.

The Hornbeak Fire Department , which is about 15 miles from the Northwest Correctional Complex, said it captured video of Morley passing in front of the fire department building in the stolen truck around 1:18 a.m.

Morley is the second inmate to escape from the Tennessee Department of Correction's custody in the past week.

Morley was convicted of first-degree murder for the killing of Cody Birchfield, who was initially reported missing in February 2022, according to the Carter County Sheriff's Office.

Birchfield's body was found in a box under Morley's house weeks after he went missing, The Associated Press reported. Morley also led police on a chase that ended in North Carolina after he found deputies at his home in 2022, according to authorities.

The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, which has added Morley to its "Most Wanted" list, is offering a reward of up to $2,500 for information leading to his arrest.

The Northwest Correctional Complex can house up to 1,776 male inmates, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction .

CNN's Amanda Jackson contributed to this report.

articles.title: An anonymous donor gave £17.5 million to buy a 7,618-hectare Scottish estate; the wildlife charity plans to restore peatlands and rainforest habitats while ending commercial grouse shooting
articles.summary: The Scottish Wildlife Trust acquired the 7,618-hectare Inverbroom Estate in the Scottish Highlands following a £17.5 million donation from an anonymous
articles.body: The Scottish Wildlife Trust acquired the 7,618-hectare Inverbroom Estate in the Scottish Highlands following a £17.5 million donation from an anonymous private donor, the largest contribution in the charity’s 60-year history. Announced on 3 March 2025, the purchase will support plans to restore wildlife habitats through woodland regeneration and peatland restoration. The trust has also committed to working with local farmers to promote sustainable agricultural practices, while creating opportunities for employment, training and volunteering. As part of its agreement with the donor, the charity confirmed that restoration work at the estate would not be funded through the sale of carbon credits.How will £17.5 million help restore Scotland’s Inverbroom EstateThe Scottish Wildlife Trust plans to restore wildlife and habitats across the Inverbroom Estate. According to Civil Society, the charity’s proposed work includes woodland regeneration and peatland restoration to transform the landscape. The estate contains some of Scotland’s recognised species and habitats, and the trust intends to manage the land for the benefit of wildlife and local communities.The charity also plans to work with local farmers to promote sustainable agricultural practices that benefit nature while maintaining a productive business model. These plans form part of the trust’s wider approach to managing the estate following its acquisition. The agreement with the anonymous donor also specifies that restoration work at Inverbroom will not be financed through carbon-credit sales.How will the Inverbroom Estate benefit wildlife and local peopleAlongside its habitat restoration plans, the Scottish Wildlife Trust has committed to acting as a responsible landlord at Inverbroom. The charity intends to develop opportunities for local people through employment, training and volunteering. Its plans also include working with farmers to encourage agricultural practices that support nature while allowing farming businesses to remain productive.The estate’s acquisition comes with a commitment to deliver benefits for both wildlife and people. In a statement reported by Civil Society, chief executive Jo Pike said the site had been secured for the benefit of Scotland’s wildlife and people, noting that overseas buyers had also expressed interest in the property. The trust’s plans combine habitat restoration with sustainable land management and opportunities for local participation.Why did the trust keep the Inverbroom Estate donor anonymousAlthough the donor has chosen to remain anonymous, the Scottish Wildlife Trust confirmed that it carried out due diligence before accepting the donation. A spokesperson told Civil Society: “Despite not disclosing the identity of the donor publicly, the trust has carried out due diligence on the donation as we would normally do.” The spokesperson explained that this included examining donors’ environmental policies and reputations, associated companies and previous giving histories.The spokesperson added that the trust was confident in its due diligence process and had previously declined donations when concerns arose over risks such as greenwashing. The charity took ownership of the majority of Inverbroom Estate on 3 March 2025, with the remainder due to transfer on 8 April. Pike described the acquisition as an important milestone for the trust and Scotland’s efforts to address nature and climate challenges. She also thanked the donor and former chief executive and current trust ambassador Jonny Hughes, who facilitated the donation.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia offered Houthis $1 billion through Iran to stop attacks: Report
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia has reportedly offered $1 billion to Yemen's Houthi group under an Iran-brokered arrangement aimed at securing a ceasefire and stopping
articles.body: Saudi Arabia has reportedly offered $1 billion to Yemen's Houthi group under an Iran-brokered arrangement aimed at securing a ceasefire and stopping attacks on the kingdom, Israeli media reported, citing diplomatic sources in the Gulf.According to the reports, Saudi defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman travelled to Tehran for talks on a possible ceasefire with the Houthis. The proposed arrangement reportedly involved transferring $1 billion to the group through Iran.One diplomatic source claimed that the Saudi minister had even brought the money to Tehran aboard the Hercules military transport aircraft he arrived in. However, a Saudi official did not confirm that any money had been transferred, the reports said.The talks reportedly brought together Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin and Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir, alongside Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Supreme National Security Council Secretary General Mohsen Rezaei and senior officials from the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).According to the reports, Iran offered to mediate between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis amid escalating attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities, which have caused economic damage to the kingdom. Iranian attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz have also disrupted oil exports from the Gulf, adding to regional instability.The Saudi foreign ministry addressed the visit in an official statement, saying, "The visit to Tehran by Prince Khalid bin Salman, the defence minister, and representatives of the member states of the Mecca Joint Defence Alliance comes as part of the 'Nato-style' alliance's ongoing efforts to de-escalate tensions between the parties to the current crisis, encourage dialogue and diplomatic solutions, and support the mediation efforts undertaken by the State of Qatar and the Islamic Republic of Pakistan."A Saudi official, speaking to Israeli media, did not confirm the reported financial transfer but said that part of the dispute with the Houthis centred on the implementation of understandings reached three years ago.Under those understandings, Saudi Arabia was to provide direct financial assistance to the Houthis as part of efforts to reach a settlement. The funding was intended, among other purposes, to pay public-sector salaries in areas under Houthi control and rebuild civilian infrastructure. In return, the group was expected to maintain the ceasefire and stop attacks on Saudi Arabia, the reports said.In recent months, the Houthis have sought to justify their "attacks" by alleging that Saudi Arabia reneged on the earlier understandings.However, the Saudi position reportedly remains that the kingdom will not agree to a new ceasefire under "military blackmail". Israeli media reported that Riyadh also opposed transferring funds to the Houthis before they returned territory seized from Yemen's internationally recognised government, which Saudi Arabia backs.The reported negotiations come amid wider regional tensions involving Iran, the United States and Israel. Tehran has sought to strengthen its regional influence while promoting a security framework led by regional powers.According to Israeli media, the Tehran meeting also marked the first official meeting between representatives of the Mecca Joint Defence Alliance and the Iranian leadership. The initiative reportedly took shape during the Pakistani army chief's visit to Tehran the previous week.The reports said Iran was seeking to position itself as a regional diplomatic mediator while opposing US or Israeli military intervention in the region.The reported $1 billion proposal, including the claim that the money was brought to Tehran aboard the Saudi minister's aircraft, has not been independently confirmed.You use AI every day. articles.title: How dispute over hotel lease escalated into mass shooting at Guwahati's Bilas Inn, with leaseholder killing 4 linked to owner's family
articles.summary: GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another
articles.body: GUWAHATI: A dispute over a hotel lease allegedly escalated into a deadly shooting in Guwahati on Monday night, leaving five people dead and another injured.The victims included the hotel's co-owner, her son and daughter-in-law, her brother and the property’s caretaker.The accused, identified as Ghanakanta Gogoi, the hotel's leaseholder, was arrested within an hour of the incident, police said.Gogoi allegedly opened fire at Hotel Bilas Inn on GS Road, opposite Bora Service, around 9pm. The hotel is about 2km from the Assam Police headquarters.The victims were associated with the hotel's ownership and management. Four of the deceased belonged to the same family, while the fifth person was from their village, Guwahati police commissioner Partha Sarathi Mahanta said. The injured survivor was also from the same village.“Preliminary investigation suggests that the incident stemmed from a property dispute related to the lease agreement of the hotel,” Mahanta told reporters outside the property.Gogoi had taken the hotel on lease about a year ago, the commissioner said, adding that investigators were examining all aspects of the incident to establish the sequence of events.Accused arrested, licensed pistol seizedPolice apprehended Gogoi in the Paltan Bazar area within an hour of the shooting. A licensed .32-bore pistol, suspected to have been used in the killings, was seized from him.“Six persons sustained gunshot wounds, of whom five succumbed to the injuries. One person is undergoing treatment,” Mahanta said.Three of the deceased have been identified as Helena Bharali, Deborshi Kashyap and Narayan Das, while the identities of the remaining victims were being verified.The sole survivor, identified as Satyen Pathak, 42, sustained a bullet injury to his shoulder and was undergoing treatment at Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. His condition was stable, a senior doctor said.A forensic and scientific investigation is underway, with specialised teams examining the crime scene and collecting evidence. Police said further investigation would establish the precise circumstances that led to the shooting.Congress raises law and order concernsAssam Congress president and Jorhat MP Gaurav Gogoi expressed grief over the killings and raised concerns about public safety in Guwahati.In a social media post, Gogoi offered condolences to the victims' families and said the incident raised serious questions about the city's law and order situation. He called on chief minister and home minister Himanta Biswa Sarma to take responsibility and pay greater attention to rising crime.Gogoi, the deputy leader of the opposition in the Lok Sabha, also called for a thorough inquiry, accountability and concrete measures to prevent similar incidents.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Israel Elections 2026 Live Updates: Polls open in Israel, voters to decide whether to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Israel is voting in parliamentary elections, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu seeking another term amid public scrutiny of his government's han
articles.body: Israel Elections 2026: Why the result matters beyond the country Israel's election carries implications for its relations with the United States, its regional security policy and its international standing. The country's alliance with Washington faces pressure amid the conflict involving Iran and continuing disagreements over the wars in the region. US President Donald Trump has publicly backed Netanyahu, making the election relevant to American political debate as well. Israel has also faced mounting international criticism over its military campaign in Gaza, while Netanyahu is subject to an International Criminal Court arrest warrant issued in 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity. The next government will face the challenge of managing security threats while navigating strained diplomatic relationships..Israel Elections: Voting begins as Eisenkot invokes October 7 attack, Netanyahu projects strongman image Voting began across Israel as 7,331,981 registered voters headed to polling stations to elect members of the Knesset. Polling is scheduled to close at 10 pm local time. Ahead of the vote, former Israel Defence Forces (IDF) chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, a key challenger to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, invoked the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack while urging voters to back his Yashar party. Meanwhile, Netanyahu projected a strongman image as he sought another term in office..Israel Elections: Palestinian issue takes a back seat in Israel's election campaign Despite the devastating impact of the Gaza war and growing international scrutiny of Israel's treatment of Palestinians, the Palestinian issue has received limited attention in Israel's election campaign. Most major contenders have not advocated reviving the long-stalled peace process or establishing a Palestinian state in the foreseeable future. Netanyahu has sought to frame the election around security and opposition to Palestinian statehood, while his rivals have criticised aspects of his leadership and raised concerns about settler violence in the occupied West Bank. Arab party leader Mansour Abbas has focused largely on crime and security in Arab communities, while positioning his party as a potential coalition partner..Israel Elections 2026: Who are the key contenders in Israel's election More than 30 parties are contesting Israel's parliamentary election, but only a smaller group is expected to secure seats in the 120-member Knesset. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu leads the right-wing Likud party, while former military chief Gadi Eisenkot heads the centrist Yashar party. Former prime minister Naftali Bennett is contesting the election alongside Yair Lapid's political camp. Other prominent figures include far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, centre-left leader Yair Golan and Arab party leader Mansour Abbas. Their performances, alliances and willingness to cooperate could prove decisive in determining who can assemble the 61 lawmakers needed to form a government..Israel Elections: Military-service exemptions emerge as key election issue The question of military service has emerged as a significant issue in Israel's election, as the country faces prolonged security demands and continuing regional tensions. Netanyahu's governing coalitions have relied on ultra-Orthodox parties that seek exemptions from compulsory military service for young men studying in religious institutions. The arrangement has drawn criticism from Israelis who believe the burden of military duty should be shared more equally. Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has pledged to end the exemptions. The issue could also shape post-election coalition negotiations, with religious parties potentially holding the balance of power in a closely divided Knesset..Israel Elections 2026: October 7 attack remains central to Israel's election The October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack continues to shape Israel's political debate as voters head to the polls. The assault killed around 1,200 people in Israel and saw 251 others abducted, triggering the war in Gaza and wider regional conflict. Security failures surrounding the attack have become a major point of contention, with Netanyahu facing criticism over accountability and his resistance to calls for a commission of inquiry. According to the Israel Democracy Institute, around 68% of Jewish Israelis consider their attitudes towards October 7 a central factor in deciding which party to support..Israel Elections: A referendum on Netanyahu's leadership Israel's parliamentary election is widely seen as a test of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's leadership, with his handling of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack and the wars that followed at the centre of the campaign. Netanyahu faces a challenge from opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief, amid public debate over security failures, military-service exemptions for ultra-Orthodox Jews and the government's policies. Polls suggest a close contest, with neither bloc assured of a parliamentary majority. The outcome could determine whether Netanyahu retains power or the opposition succeeds in forming a new government.

articles.title: Forest of Dean prepper has 'enough food to last for 12 months'
articles.summary: As the government warns the public to have a store of supplies ready in case of emergency, one man needs no telling.
articles.body:
Advice was issued by the government last week in a bid to encourage us all to stock up on supplies in case of a national emergency.

They said households should have three days' supply to make sure they have what they need to get through any "rocky" periods .

One man who needs no telling to prepare is forager and gardener Shane whose terraced house on a quiet Forest of Dean street looks like any other.

But behind his front door there are hundreds of jars, bottles and packets of food stacked high and hidden in every room.

"I've got enough food to last for 12 months definitely, with what we grow in the garden, all of our solar [power] and the springs, we should do all right," says Shane, who declined to give his surname.

Shane is what is known as a prepper - someone who has stocks of food, water and non-mains energy sources - in case of a catastrophic disaster.

He has been prepping for more than 20 years, predominantly to cope with power outages and road closures which affect rural areas of the Forest of Dean at times of extreme weather but more recently because of global tensions.

Recently, however, Shane has noticed an increase in people asking him about prepping, especially those concerned with the rising frequency of extreme weather events and the threat of cyber attacks on critical networks such as food supply chains.

We're just tax-collectors, say pub landlords asking for help

Two teachers struck off for encouraging pupils to fight

Road closure fears for shops and hospital access

"It seems to be now there are threats from AI, cyber attacks, there's crop failures, there's supermarket prices shooting up, there's even a threat from Russia and China - so they all seem to be coming to a head now," he says.

"A lot of people are getting quite frightened about it so it's a good time, I think, just to get yourself ready."

Shane's main consideration while prepping is storage.

He uses a chest in his living room to store shop-bought products such as honey and custard. It is metal to prevent mice getting in.

He has filing cabinets filled with jars of preserves which he self-cans and areas dedicated to dehydrated goods such as chillies, which he says will last for years.

Spaces behind doors and sofas is given over to keeping various camping stoves, solar-powered lights and batteries.

He also has a gravity shower which will enable him to wash if the mains water is off as well as a wood-burner to warm up a kettle of water.

Shane's cupboards and drawers are stuffed to bursting with all sorts of tempting and unusual foods, including leek and potato soup and chicken Rogan Josh curries.

In fact Shane is confident he can preserve almost anything - with the exception of dairy which he says would curdle.

"A lot of people say about storing rice and beans but if you're feeling miserable anyway, why do you want to store rice and beans?

"You can buy puddings and fruit in tins, cereal bars keep for a long time - just get something you can enjoy rather than the bare, basic, gritty stuff," he says.

Shane, who has written a number of books about specialist fruit and vegetables, says he operates a strict system when it comes to food with expiry dates.

"You always try to sort of rotate and keep an eye on the dates," he says.

"Some things will keep longer - chutneys will keep for two or three years, pickles maybe a year, meat and fish a year as well.

"And if you've got to use them, replace them, so you've always got that same amount in store all the time."

And while it may seem like a lot of effort, he says that "after a while it just becomes second nature".

During the Cold War the UK government ran a series of Protect and Survive campaigns which encouraged households to keep supplies in a special 'fall out room'.

And official food reserves were kept in 60 secret locations across the country until the mid-90s.

In Europe many places still advise the public to keep up to 10 days of supplies in case of emergencies.

While there is no immediate widescale public threat, the government last week launched a "national resilience conversation".

This includes a 'be ready checklist' which states households should have an emergency kit containing enough food, water and medication to last for three days as well as cash, a battery and a wind-up radio.

The Cabinet Office said the campaign would build over the next three years.

Councillors in Gloucestershire are also calling for more to be done to increase emergency food and energy resilience at a local level.

Stroud District Council leader and county councillor Chloe Turner has asked for more thought to be put into a local plan for the county.

"We need to be thinking about a system change and what local authorities and what government can do to support people if there is a crisis," she says.

"That might be a crisis of getting food in to the country but it might also be a crisis about how we distribute food and how we store food and how we actually get it to people."

For Shane, his prepping will continue in earnest and, while he is more than happy to offer advice, he is not looking for any new housemates.

"So many people say to me, 'if things go wrong, I'm coming to live with you'," he says.

"But it's only a little house and there's only so many people we can fit in."
